messages.text:
The Magic M. 40T is $799 and runs about 40 TH/s — our best value per terahash right now. Most people buy it for the shot at a full block plus steady sats to their own wallet.

What do you pay per kWh?

Solar changes the math in your favour — the 40T draws about 650 W at 40 TH/s, roughly 15.6 kWh a day, and it drops to 450 W in Eco mode if you want it to live inside your array.

Is it running daytime-only off the panels, or do you have battery to carry it overnight?

2.4 kW peak — the 40T at 650 W sits comfortably inside that with room for the house, and Eco mode at 450 W covers cloudy days. On panels you're effectively mining on free power, so every sat it stacks is yours to keep, plus a full-block draw every ten minutes.

That's the one I'd get: Magic M. 40T, $799, Batch 6, ships November 21, 2026. Want me to set up the checkout?
can it lower itself at night to not drain battery

Honestly: the 40T has three modes — 450 W, 650 W, 850 W — and you switch them in its dashboard. Whether it can drop modes automatically on a schedule or off a battery signal, I don't want to guess at.

Plenty of people handle it with a smart plug or their inverter's load control instead, which cuts it off cleanly at dusk.

I've put the auto-throttle question to our hardware guy — the team picks it up Monday at 10am ET and the answer comes to your email. Want the email it should go to?
Handed to the team · auto-throttle / scheduling cap···· the MM40T is not in the product facts

B30 is $899 for 30 TH/s at 360–450 W. The 40T is $799 for 40 TH/s at 650 W, and it tunes down to 30 TH/s at 450 W — so at the B30's power draw you get the same hashrate for $100 less, with headroom to push to 50 TH/s when the sun is strong.

On a 2.4 kW array that flexibility is the whole argument. I'd still take the 40T. B30 ships November 30, 2026; the 40T ships November 21, 2026.
